title: page.look names the rule that really wins a shorthand (padding, margin, border-radius…) side by side, and look.set beats every rule that wins a part of it
steps: S1: From packages/tools/tracy-site-tools run: node --test --test-reporter=tap test/look-style.test.mjs test/look-set.test.mjs

S2: Read the result of the tests named in run.tests: resolveStyles on the dskeepwp hero button cascade (test/look-cascade-fixture.mjs — global styles' own padding-* (0,1,0), the agent's `padding:14px 25px` (0,7,0), the design-system slot's padding-top/-right/-bottom/-left (0,8,0)), and look.set on the readings it makes.
expect: page.look's `padding` names the slot's `:root:root:root:root:root:root .tracy .wp-block-button__link` with set 'padding-top: 7px; padding-right: 21px; padding-bottom: 7px; padding-left: 21px' — never the agent's losing shorthand rule; `padding-top` and a shorthand-vs-shorthand `border-radius` read as before.

When different rules win different sides, `parts` names each group with its rule and sheet, the latest in the cascade leads, a side no rule sets is its own part, and the answer's next says a change must beat each.

look.set scope element writes a rule more specific than (0,8,0) holding `padding: 14px 25px`; scope site refuses a shorthand split across rules (naming each) and, for one rule setting its sides from tokens, appends the shorthand to that rule and sets no token to a two-value padding.
evidence: dskeepwp 09/10/2026: the slot wrote padding-top/-bottom:7px, padding-left/-right:21px at (0,8,0); the agent's Additional CSS `padding:14px 25px` (0,7,0) lost, computed stayed 7px 21px, page.look named the agent's rule as the winner and the agent told the customer the button was bigger.
fence: resolveStyles resolves a shorthand longhand by longhand (namesFor covers every shorthand of a longhand); look.set beats the most specific winner at or after the latest sheet

tests: 🔒 a shorthand is read side by side
a shorthand whose sides different rules win: each group named
🔒 WordPress wearing a design system: a padding change beats the slot
a shorthand whose sides different rules win: the element rule beats the most specific
scope "site" on a shorthand its rule sets side by side from tokens
